plain_text:
MOST OF US KNOW that eating
fruits and vegetables is good for our
health. But a new study from the
National Institutes of Health says it may
even help us live longer.
semantic_text: MOST OF US KNOW that eating fruits and vegetables is good for our health. But a new study from the National Institutes of Health says it may even help us live longer.

plain_text:
The study found that eating an
average of five servings of fruits and
vegetables a day is linked to a reduced
risk of death from heart and respiratory
diseases. Eating more fruit is also
associated with a lower risk of cancer.
semantic_text: The study found that eating an average of five servings of fruits and vegetables a day is linked to a reduced risk of death from heart and respiratory diseases. Eating more fruit is also associated with a lower risk of cancer.

plain_text:
Researchers gathered data from
more than 100,000 people starting in
the mid-1980s until 2014. Participants
included people who didn’t have
diabetes, heart disease, or cancer when
the study began. All participants were
asked questions about their diets every
two to four years.
semantic_text: Researchers gathered data from more than 100,000 people starting in the mid-1980s until 2014. Participants included people who didn’t have diabetes, heart disease, or cancer when the study began. All participants were asked questions about their diets every two to four years.

plain_text:
The results showed that eating about
two servings of fruit and three servings
of vegetables a day was associated with
lower risk of death from chronic disease.
semantic_text: The results showed that eating about two servings of fruit and three servings of vegetables a day was associated with lower risk of death from chronic disease.

plain_text:
Most types of fruits and vegetables
led to these results, except fruit juices
and starchy vegetables such as peas,
corn, and potatoes. Although it is often
recommended to eat 5 cups of fruits
and vegetables a day, eating more than

plain_text:
five servings per day wasn't associated
with further reduction in risk of death.

plain_text:
Researchers in this study added their
findings to data from 26 other studies.
The combined findings support
current daily recommendations
for eating fruits and vegetables.
For adults, the recommended daily
amount is 1.5 to 2 cups of fruit and 2
to 3 cups of vegetables.
semantic_text: Researchers in this study added their findings to data from 26 other studies. The combined findings support current daily recommendations for eating fruits and vegetables. For adults, the recommended daily amount is 1.5 to 2 cups of fruit and 2 to 3 cups of vegetables.

plain_text:
However, the average American adult
only eats about one serving of fruit
and 1.5 servings of vegetables a day. So,
the next time you head to a grocery
store, make sure to add some apples,
broccoli, or whatever healthy options
you like to your cart!
semantic_text: However, the average American adult only eats about one serving of fruit and 1.5 servings of vegetables a day. So, the next time you head to a grocery store, make sure to add some apples, broccoli, or whatever healthy options you like to your cart!
SOURCES: National Cancer Institute; National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute; National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
